frontier.hypothesis: D4 (4 of the remaining 8 points) - the walker init must be emitted LAST in the preheader (target: `addu $t0,$zero,$zero ; addiu $t4,zero,<w> ; addiu $t2,zero,0x20 ; addu $t1,$t3,$zero`) without losing the walker's live range.
frontier.mechanism: Moving the init late in SOURCE is measured dead at three allocations (31 at floor 20, 27 at floor 12, 23 at floor 8) because it shortens the walker's livelen and lifts it above the loop counter in global.c allocno_compare (counter nrefs 21 / livelen 60 / pri 14000; walkers nrefs 13). The init position itself is otherwise pure source order.
frontier.next_probe: Move the init late AND pay the livelen back from the OTHER end: give `dst` a reference after loop 1 and `dst2` a reference after loop 2, so the live range is restored without the early init. If that fails, execute the reading no session has done - tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c move_movables / scan_loop - to establish whether the walker init is a movable at all in this form and where the preheader insertion point is chosen relative to the loop's first insn.

frontier.hypothesis: D5 (4 of the remaining 8 points) - target schedules `sllv $a2,$a2,$a0` (`cur <<= needed`) before the `or`; we emit the `or` first. It is a list-scheduler tie-break, not a source-order effect.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c INSN_PRIORITY / ready-list ordering. Session 5 proved statement order neutral (vTieShiftEarly, bit-identical residual), so the decision is made inside sched.c.
frontier.next_probe: Point tools/sched_solver (validated 6978/6978, memory/project/sched-solver-campaign-2026-08-05.md) at the refill arm's block in both our build and target, identify the priority/tie-break that orders the `or` against the `sllv`, then derive which C-visible change (an extra dependence into `cur`, a different consumer distance) moves it. The .sched / .sched2 -da dumps for the current form are reproducible with tmp/grind/func_8001979C/s6/dump.sh.
